manifest.name: dsh-workspace-cleaner
manifest.description: Workspace and session cleanup for DeepSeek Harness: a settings page listing every workspace with its session count, and a sidebar session menu row that really deletes a session log (into a recoverable trash).

readme.text:
Workspace and session cleanup for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai) — a settings page that lists every workspace registration with its session count, plus a **delete session** row in the sidebar's session menu that really removes the log (into a recoverable trash).

> Git 版说明见 [README.zh.md](README.zh.md)。

DSH deliberately ships no session deletion. The JSONL persistence backend documents it plainly:

> **Nothing deletes session files** — logs accumulate under `root` until removed externally; the seam has no deletion API.

So the sidebar's session menu only offers **Archive**. Once a few hundred sessions pile up, the sidebar becomes unmanageable and the logs keep growing on disk. This plugin fills the two gaps:

1. **Settings → Workspace Cleanup** — one table of every workspace: its path, session count, whether the directory still exists, bulk archive of its sessions, and deletion of the workspace registration.
2. **Session menu → Delete session** — moves that session's log directory into a trash folder, hides the sidebar row immediately, and offers restore/permanent deletion from the settings page.

Nothing is unlinked on the first click: deletion is a **rename**, so it stays recoverable.

readme.section: from the directory that contains this package
readme.text:
dsh plugin add /absolute/path/to/dsh-workspace-cleaner
```

Or, inside a DSH session, ask the agent to install the bundle from the local directory; `plugin_manager install_bundle` links the checkout into the profile (`node_modules/dsh-workspace-cleaner`), so later edits to the files need only a restart.

Restart DSH after installing (the Host half registers HTTP routes), then reload the Web GUI.

- **Deleting a live session is refused**: its writer still owns the log. Switch to another session first.
- The row disappears immediately — deletion archives the session (what the sidebar filters on) *before* moving the log, because the registry's in-memory session index would otherwise keep listing the file until a restart.
- The log directory is renamed to `<dsh-home>/session-trash/<timestamp>--<session-id>/` with a `meta.json` recording the title, project directory, cwd and deletion time.

| Action | Effect |
|---|---|
| Archive sessions (per workspace / bulk) | `workspaceRegistry.archiveSession` — sessions leave the grouped list, recoverable from the archived list |
| Delete workspace (per workspace / bulk) | `workspaceRegistry.delete` — drops the registration only; session logs, directories and files stay |
| Trash → Restore | Moves the log back, unarchives the session and re-attaches it to its workspace |
| Trash → Delete permanently | Removes the trashed directory for good and reports the freed bytes |

```
client.js  ──POST /workspace-cleaner/api/{list,apply,trash,deleteSession,restore,purge}──►  index.js
   (settings.section page + sidebar session menu row)                                    (Host: workspaceRegistry,
                                                                                           sessionPersistence,
                                                                                           node:fs over the log root)

- The **Host half** owns every operation and exposes them over one JSON route guarded by the same browser-trust fence as the shipped browser routes (`ctx.connection.requestRejection`). It is the only part that touches the filesystem.
- The **Client half** registers two slots: a `settings.section` page (`Workspace Cleanup`) and one row in `sidebar.workspaces.session.menu.item` (`Delete session`, order 500, after the shipped rows). All text goes through the locale service (`zh` / `en`), and all styling uses `--dsw-alias-*` theme tokens.
- Data comes from the Host rather than the Client's `ctx.workspaces` face, because that face can only mutate a workspace it is already given — it cannot enumerate them for a plugin page.

The JSONL backend's documented layout is:

```text
<root>/
  --<normalized-cwd>--/
    <session-id>/
      session.v4.jsonl.zstd

`<root>` is resolved from the first candidate that exists and holds project directories:

1. `config.sessionRoot` (see below)
2. `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/../../sessions`
3. `$DSH_PROFILE_DIR/sessions`
4. `$DSH_HOME/sessions`
5. `~/.dsh/sessions`

A session is matched by its own directory name, and the directory must contain `session*.jsonl[.zstd]`.

```yaml
- id: workspace-cleaner
  name: dsh-workspace-cleaner
  config:
    sessionRoot: 'D:\somewhere\session-logs'   # optional override

| Field | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `sessionRoot` | auto-discovered | Absolute path of the JSONL session-log root |

- A **live Agent** (`ctx.agents.get(id)`) is refused with `409 session/live`.
- A missing log is **not an error**: the session was either never materialized (nothing on disk) or already deleted; the accounting is cleaned and the caller gets `unmaterialized` / `alreadyDeleted` instead of a failure.
- A failed rename **rolls back the archive**, so the row never claims a deletion that did not happen.
- Trash entry ids are validated (no `..`, no separators) before any path is built.
- Deleting the currently open session is refused — it is always live.

- A session deleted while its row is still cached in the GUI needs a page reload/restart to drop from the *archived* list; the grouped list updates immediately.
- The SQLite search index can hold a stale hit for a deleted session until the next DSH start.
- Session directories are matched by id; ids containing characters the backend escapes differently would report "no session log on disk".
- The trash lives beside the log root (`<dsh-home>/session-trash`) so the backend never scans it.

No build step: plain ESM, plain browser module.

```bash
node .verify-host.mjs     # Host route + real filesystem (delete/restore/purge) — 58 checks
node .verify-client.mjs   # both slot components under a tiny hook renderer — 67 checks
```
